evidence: A three-minim arched group and a round bowl whose right stem descends and sweeps back left in a long heavy stroke under the group; the hooked tail at the left edge is the end of a large sweeping stroke from the preceding sign and the upright crossing the top right is a descender from the line above, neither counted.

A crossed upright whose bar runs without a lift into a zigzag stroke dropping to a lower loop (the zigzag-with-lower-loop shape also stands alone elsewhere on the page), a small closed loop with a long hairline rising up-right, and a large sweeping stroke entering from above the crop that ends in an upturned terminal hook; 3 if the crossed upright and its zigzag are one sign; the mark on the bottom edge is from the line below.

A crossed upright joined at its bar to a zigzag stroke with a lower loop, a two-arch minim group, and a tall looped stroke rising from the last minim that arches over and descends to an upturned terminal hook (the same arching shape stands alone elsewhere); 3 if the crossed upright and zigzag are one sign; the faint arc at the top is a descender from the line above.

A crossed upright joined to a zigzag stroke with a lower loop, then a small closed loop whose hairline rises up-right to a hook; the right edge cuts through the left half of a double-barred sign that continues into the neighbouring box (not counted); 2 if the crossed upright and zigzag are one sign.
A single group of three evenly spaced arched minims with a hairline lead-in from the left, no break or change of stroke shape inside it; the same three-minim group recurs as a unit across the page.

A minim group of three downstrokes (the first hooked) and a round bowl whose right stem descends and sweeps back left in a long heavy stroke under the group; the short stroke leaving the bowl top to the right is the join to the next sign.

A minim group with a lead-in, then a figure with a hooked top curving down into a lower closed loop (crossed at mid-height by the joining hairline), then a small double loop with a pointed upper loop whose exit stroke runs to the right edge toward the next sign.

Same sequence as L06_b028: a crossed upright joined to a zigzag with a lower loop, a small closed loop whose hairline rises into a large arch, and that arch (starting with its own hook inside the box) descending to an upturned terminal hook; 3 if the crossed upright and zigzag are one sign; the mark on the bottom edge is from the line below.

A three-minim group, then a heavy diagonal with a hooked start at upper left running down-right into a small slanted eyelet, from whose lower left a descender drops and sweeps back left to a heavy end; the eyelet with swept descender also stands alone elsewhere on the page and the hooked diagonal matches the arching sign seen elsewhere without it, so read as two signs joined without a lift (2 if one compound sign); the thin hairline at top left and the blob at the top are traces from the line above.

A small sign of two crossing strokes at the left edge with a long hairline running up-right from it to a round bowl whose right stem descends and sweeps back left in a heavy stroke, then a two-minim cup with an exit stroke to the right.

Two small closed loops joined by hairlines, then a heavy diagonal entering from above the crop into a small slanted eyelet with a thin descender dropping from the junction and turning into a heavy leftward base stroke; same diagonal-eyelet-descender junction as L23_b006, read as two joined signs (3 if one compound sign); the curved mark at top left is from the line above.

Most of a zigzag stroke whose lower loop is cut off at the lower left (its crossed upright lies outside to the left) and one complete three-minim group; the right edge holds the start of a crossed stroke belonging to the next sign, not counted.

A tall upright with a hooked head curving right and a thickened middle that runs past both the top and bottom of the crop, then a crossed upright joined at its bar to a zigzag stroke ending in a lower curl; a sliver of the neighbouring sign's tall stem shows at the left edge; 2 if the crossed upright and zigzag are one sign.

A crisp sign of two crossing curved strokes with, fused to its left lobe, a diffuse soft-edged upright mark that looks smudged or blotted rather than a clean pen stroke (1 if it is a blot); a single minim at the right edge is the first stroke of a minim group that continues outside the box and the dark stroke at the bottom right corner is part of the next sign's descender, neither counted.

A small serpentine stroke at the left, then a long thin hairline rising from the lower left into a pointed two-peak zigzag that runs into a small slanted eyelet with a descender sweeping back left to a heavy end; the eyelet with swept descender also stands alone elsewhere, so read as two joined signs after the serpentine one (2 if the zigzag-eyelet-descender unit, which recurs identically on line 23, is one compound sign); the blob at the top edge is from the line above.

A minim group of three downstrokes, the third pointed and rising without a lift into an upright with a closed loop at its upper right and a descender below the line; the same three-stroke-into-looped-upright join recurs on line 27 (3 if the pointed third stroke is its own sign); a sliver of the preceding zigzag at the left edge and a descender arc from the line above are not counted.
